blocks: MIIT General Office, Information and Communications Administration, Document No. 42 (2026)

“Agent terminal” means telecommunications terminal equipment — mobile phones, tablets, wearable devices and the like — on which an agent is pre-installed. In order to thoroughly implement the spirit of the Party’s 20th National Congress and of the successive plenary sessions of the 20th Central Committee, to coordinate development and security, to promote the healthy and orderly development of agent terminals, and to effectively safeguard the lawful rights and interests of users, and pursuant to the Cybersecurity Law of the People’s Republic of China, the Data Security Law of the People’s Republic of China, the Personal Information Protection Law of the People’s Republic of China, the Anti‑Telecom and Online Fraud Law of the People’s Republic of China, the Telecommunications Regulations of the People’s Republic of China, the Measures for the Administration of Network Access of Telecommunications Equipment and other relevant laws, regulations and rules, notice is hereby given of the following matters.

(1) Carry out agent–terminal adaptation. An “agent” is an intelligent system possessing the capabilities of autonomous perception, memory, decision‑making, interaction and execution. Agent developers shall strengthen adaptation verification with terminal equipment and tighten management of permission invocation, communications capability, network and data security, user rights and interests, and task execution, so as to ensure conformity with regulatory requirements and with user expectations and to guarantee that agents run compatibly and stably. Agent developers shall standardise the management of agent information and shall publish an adaptation verification list to users on the product settings page, specifying the terminal models for which adaptation has been completed together with operating system information, so as to safeguard users’ right to know and right to choose. Before an agent is listed on an app distribution platform, its developer shall submit the status of its adaptation verification to that platform.

(2) Improve network‑access administration for agent terminals. Risk assessments shall be conducted, the testing regime for network access of telecommunications equipment shall be refined, and the requirements for matters subject to special provisions shall be made more specific. Agent terminals such as mobile phones, tablets and wearable devices on which agents are pre-installed must undergo agent adaptation verification against the relevant standards as part of network‑access testing; fraud‑risk security assessments and ex ante anti‑fraud capability evaluations of agent terminals shall be carried out in accordance with law, and the requirements for priority communications work shall be implemented. Agents used on terminals shall be furnished with a unique identity code by reference to the national standards series on agent interconnection. Terminal manufacturers shall ensure the consistency of an agent terminal before and after it obtains its network access licence. Where an agent terminal undergoes a material change, the terminal manufacturer shall file a report with the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and conduct network‑access testing as required.

(3) Strengthen management of live‑network agent upgrades. Where a terminal manufacturer performs a live‑network agent upgrade by over‑the‑air (OTA) push or other means, it shall submit a live‑network upgrade plan to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology specifying the timing, scale, user population, business scenarios, service content, business model, network and data security measures, and anti‑telecom‑and‑online‑fraud measures of the upgrade, and shall concurrently attend to priority communications work. After the live‑network upgrade is complete, the terminal manufacturer shall submit a live‑network upgrade report to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, and may formally provide the service to users only after the Ministry has organised expert assessment and solicited opinions.

(4) Improve the mechanism for administering agent distribution. App distribution platforms shall require application developers to declare affirmatively, by electronic signature, whether they consent to invocation by agents; absent a declared consent, an agent may not compulsorily invoke or call the application. App distribution platforms shall publish the agent adaptation verification list to users on the distribution page, and may not provide users with download or installation services for an agent on an incompatible device model. App distribution platforms shall strengthen patrol inspection of the adaptation verification status of listed agents, and shall take measures such as rectification within a set period or delisting in respect of agents that have not completed adaptation verification.

(1) Strengthen market oversight. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and the communications administrations of the provinces, autonomous regions and directly governed municipalities shall strengthen organisation, coordination, supervision and inspection, establish routine and special inspection mechanisms, provide policy interpretation, keep complaint and reporting channels open, deal with conduct such as the placing of non‑compliant products on the market in accordance with law, and effectively safeguard the lawful rights and interests of users.

(2) Reinforce the discharge of responsibility. Each relevant entity shall effectively discharge its primary responsibility, strictly implement every task in this Notice, and conscientiously organise network‑access testing, adaptation verification, live‑network upgrades, distribution management and related work for agent terminals. It shall refine the division of tasks, clarify work objectives, and strengthen internal management and technical support, so as to ensure that every link is carried through.

(3) Consolidate capacity building. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology shall organise the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology and other relevant institutions to deepen research on agent terminal technology on an ongoing basis, and to consolidate capabilities in new‑technology analysis and test verification, incident monitoring and analysis, problem assessment and disposal, and scenario research and application. It shall organise the construction of an adaptation library of agent versions and terminal models, accelerate the formulation of standards relating to adaptation verification, accelerate the construction of a trusted identity system and management platform for agents, and continuously raise the technical and innovation level of terminals.
General Office, Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
